# Local Recon — deepening the optimization angle (architecture + algorithm)

Topic: deepen the optimization angle — both how the optimizer backend could be
architected and what algorithm improvements are available. The user added
papers/ PDFs (DIRECT-GLh, DIRECT 2022 study, Laine rasterization, Modular
Primitives) to read; more Zotero PDFs available on request; do NOT move PDFs.

## Tech stack / environment

- Qt6 (qt6-main/wayland 6.7.2) + VTK 9.3 + CUDA 12.4 + OpenCV, C++20, pixi build, jj VCS, xcb-only rendering. GPU baseline measured on an RTX 3090 (no cross-GPU noise-floor data).
- Layers: jtml_domain (pure, Qt-free) / jtml_services / jtml_coordinator (QObject) / jtml_compute (SHARED, GPU) / jtml_view / app + QML experimental app. Headless tests default; oracle/render labels excluded.

## Current optimizer architecture (verified)

- DirectOptimizer (include/domain/direct_optimizer.h, src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp): classic DIRECT — Jarvis convex-hull POH selection (epsilon=0), trisection along largest denormalized side, center sampling, L2 size measure, injected std::function cost, cooperative Stop, SetCallOffset for cumulative budgets, iteration/improvement callbacks.
- Budget shape (baseline.json, authoritative): trunk 20000, branch 2x5000, leaf 5000; cumulative effective 20k/25k/30k/35k; ranges trunk 35, branch 15 (z 25), leaf 3 (z 15); dilation trunk 6 / branch 4 (settings_constants) vs 3 (golden_oracle prose — contradiction) / leaf 1.
- Cost path: CostFunctionManager (7 registered variants: sym_trap_function, DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_SAME_Z, DIRECT_DILATION_T1, DIRECT_DILATION, DIRECT_MAHFOUZ); per-eval pipeline ~15 kernel launches + ~5 synchronous D2H memcpys (render engine ~8 kernels + 2 D2H; fast_implant_dilation 4 kernels + 1 D2H; distance_map 2+ D2H) — synthesis item 8 (sync-bound, not kernel-bound) confirmed by source count. nvtx declared in pixi.toml but zero instrumentation.
- Seams ready (plan 006): OptimizerRunDriver + OptimizerRunLaunch (full run payload by value incl. 3 CostFunctionManagers) + CreateOptimizerManagerRunDriver — the multi-stage oracle's entry point; RunDirectStage's injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+) is the z-profile probe entry; DirectOptimizer injected cost.
- Stage guard bug makes stage_ always Trunk (T1 non-trunk path unreachable). Dilation handled per stage in OptimizerManager (re-dilate), not in DirectOptimizer.

## 7 verified cost-path bugs (synthesis item 1 — pin-first)

1. DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134 — uninitialized min_dist (+= before init, UB).
2. DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:120-122 — Y_dist byte-identical to X_dist (Y_TRANS no-op).
3. sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108 — tibia transform x replaced by z.
4. CostFunctionManager.cpp:46 — always-true stage guard (stage always Trunk).
5. distance_map_metric.cu:27 — index formula (blockIdx.y + gridDim.x + ...) instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x.
6. implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324,446 — pointer-vs-value guard (always true, div-by-zero risk); double->int atomicAdd truncation.
7. curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu — stub returning 0 (kernel launched, result discarded; heatmaps uploaded unconditionally).
Dead duplicate chamfer call commented out in DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:101-104.
Determinism contradiction: all active cost-path reductions are int atomicAdd, yet docs claim atomics aren't bit-reproducible. Backface divergence: production use_backface_culling=true; oracle/parity false.

## Measurement apparatus (exists vs needed)

Exists: baseline.json (IoU 0.85 hard gate; measured 0.9936 IoU, per-px L1 0.0207, z gap 6.31 mm informational); fem_golden.jts 3-frame golden; calibration.txt; fem_oracle_captured.jtak; oracle_test (3 frames, single trunk DIRECT_DILATION, flat budget 3000, backface OFF — NOT production shape; leaf z-refinement never exercised by any test); qml_parity_check (app wiring, same config); segmentation_oracle (clean-skips without .pt); Tier-1 analytic golden (quadratic only + budget/determinism/offset pins); hegel PBT twins.
Missing: headless Tier-0 (no CPU metric-semantics tests — test_cost_function covers only the parameter registry); per-variant ablation runner + ablation.json; z-profile probe harness; CPU fallback; gpu ctest label; GPU CI; cross-GPU noise-floor; More & Wild data profiles.

## Papers shortlist (see papers/ recon for citations)

- DIRECT-GLh: hidden-constraint surrogate phi = f_min + d(x_min, x) (normalized) for infeasible points — keeps exploration at the feasibility boundary (relevant: unrenderable poses / NaN silhouette).
- 2022 study (12 variants): GL selection wins at large budgets (>= ~4k evals), IO wins small; 1-DTDV diagonal-vertex sampling dramatically best for boundary optima (2 evals vs 77-100); over-refinement restrictions HURT cheap functions (optimum ~0) — only -gb globally-biased helps expensive objectives.
- Laine 2011: fast silhouette-only software rasterizer patterns (coverage-only mode 20-30% faster, LUT masks, tile z-cull).
- Modular Primitives: differentiable rasterization primitives, occlusion-aware silhouette gradients, NDC depth z/w channel (z-axis signal!), analytic AA; inverse-rendering pose fitting at megapixel res — gradient polish after DIRECT global phase (thesis: ~12x fewer evals on engineering problems).

## Roadmap status (synthesis.org items)

1 (bugs) NOT DONE, 2 (ablation harness) NOT DONE, 3 (multi-stage oracle) NOT DONE — driver seam ready, 4 (determinism) NOT DONE, 5 (DIRECT variant switch + analytic battery) NOT DONE, 6 (z remedies) NOT DONE, 7 (dilation ablation) NOT DONE, 8 (compute perf) NOT DONE, 9 (torch cleanup) NOT DONE, 10 (ML pathway) NOT DONE, 11 (fixtures) PARTIAL, 12 (QML NO-GO) DONE, 13 (regulatory) NOT DONE. Plan-006 recommended sequence: deferred quirk cuts → item 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 → 8. Plan 006 itself complete.

## Conventions

- Layer purity (domain Qt-free), explicit .cpp lists in CMake, R13-style pin-first (characterize before changing), hegel PBT next to deterministic tests, oracle IoU >= 0.85 as the appearance gate (never raw pose — DIRECT convergence noisy), jj commits per logical change, xcb-only, jj diff not usable in the user's terminal (avoid interactive pagers).

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 2 (wave 2 complete) — all six angles carry '## Round 2' sections; wave 1 = angles 01–04, wave 2 = angles 05–06
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

Round 2 wave 2 added two more high-value deliverables on top of the wave-1 deepening. **First, the ms/call meter carries a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot**: grep finds zero CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere in src/ — both meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame and :1272-1279 iteration callback) divide raw clock() ticks by calls and label the result "ms/call"; on Linux glibc clock() returns microseconds, so the value is CPU-µs/call labeled as ms/call. The UI compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) reads the µs value as ms → IPS understated ~1000×, and the ETA (:4598/:4659) is overstated by the same factor. This is a correctness fact, not polish — no before/after perf claim through the existing meter is meaningful, and Cut 4 (now a full spec for BOTH sites) must emit true ms/call so the existing UI math becomes correct without UI changes. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1/R2-2] **Second, the polish stage is now an executable MVP spec with its own falsifiable preconditions**: a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the same 31 renders, pre-registered thresholds G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1), a forward-difference arm (7 renders/accepted step, ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), an analytic arm (1 render/step via the 2×6 projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel, with an ordered two-pass float reduction so the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin cannot trip), and a **three-arm study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k budget-gift control, C: DIRECT@34k + polish@1000)** that arbitrates the 12x-vs-1.5–3x contradiction without confounding "polish quality" with "budget reallocation". [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org R2-1/R2-2/R2-4/R2-5]

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and now fully specified in content: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (now an executable 31-render spec that also arbitrates the polish precondition G1–G4 via its term-decomposition mode) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam, which **no longer needs the "small seam addition"**: Round 2 proved Directive::SymTrap already exists in the typed enum, so the tibia-ambiguity pass is three pins, not a code change; * Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

Round 2 wave 2 added two more high-value deliverables on top of the wave-1 deepening. **First, the ms/call meter carries a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot**: grep finds zero CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere in src/ — both meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame and :1272-1279 iteration callback) divide raw clock() ticks by calls and label the result "ms/call"; on Linux glibc clock() returns microseconds, so the value is CPU-µs/call labeled as ms/call. The UI compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) reads the µs value as ms → IPS understated ~1000×, and the ETA (:4598/:4659) is overstated by the same factor. This is a correctness fact, not polish — no before/after perf claim through the existing meter is meaningful, and Cut 4 (now a full spec for BOTH sites) must emit true ms/call so the existing UI math becomes correct without UI changes. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1/R2-2] **Second, the polish stage is now an executable MVP spec with its own falsifiable preconditions**: a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the same 31 renders, pre-registered thresholds G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1), a forward-difference arm (7 renders/accepted step, ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), an analytic arm (1 render/step via the 2×6 projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel, with an ordered two-pass float reduction so the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin cannot trip), and a **three-arm study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k budget-gift control, C: DIRECT@34k + polish@1000)** that arbitrates the 12x-vs-1.5–3x contradiction without confounding "polish quality" with "budget reallocation". Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: Round 2 resolved this from a scoping tension into an explicit mechanism analysis — the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. The real z remedies remain biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's Round-2 seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state (compute owns the buffer state, the manager owns the object graph, the domain sees only std::function). Wave 2 extends this doctrine to the polish: the gradient must use an ordered (non-atomic) float reduction, because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin would trip on float-atomic accumulation.

Round 2 also closed the run's longest-standing open question: **the DIRECT-GLh NaN trigger is now resolved per-variant.** DIRECT_DILATION is structurally incapable of emitting NaN/Inf (all-int composition, +0.1-guarded division, max accumulation 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹) — the GLh trigger lives in DIRECT_MAHFOUZ (0/0 via the pointer-guard bug, production-reachable), DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (UB min_dist), and sym_trap (asin domain). The finite-check belongs at the one shared chokepoint, DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205), and the round-1 claim that "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons" is corrected: NaN boxes accumulate as dead weight at the column front (lost evals, unbounded growth), with the column minimum poisoned only after all finite boxes are trisected away — a delayed, conditional effect, still worth closing. The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis remains a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase, with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal — and wave 2's three-arm study is the instrument that will measure it. Everything else from the papers — 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — stays conditional, deferred, or NO-GO, and each lands only through the harness.

** Finding 4 — The z-weak axis is an observability limit, not an algorithm problem; the probe is the arbiter, and the real remedies are biplane or a known-geometry prior
- The 6.31 mm z gap (vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane) is the run's load-bearing research problem, converged from prior runs. The mechanism: a z shift is pure magnification — at ~1.1 m source distance a ±15 mm shift changes scale by <1%, inside the 6 px dilation tolerance; the dilated-overlap family is nearly flat in z. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "z-profile probe"; local-recon.org]
- Round 2 made the probe an executable spec: entry points verified (RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda optimizer_manager.cpp:1235-1246; public twin EvaluateCostFunctionAtPoint :1372-1387; compute-only oracle twin oracle_test.cpp:286-291); sweep Δz ∈ {−15,…,+15} mm at fixed truth = 31 renders per (variant, dilation, frame); metrics valley_depth = (max−cost(0))/(max−min), argmin_offset, plateau_halfwidth, noise_floor (5 repeats of cost(0), expect 0 for the int-atomic path); assertions p1–p4 including the ranking hypothesis asserted pin-first (nightly run 1 records, later runs enforce) and z_gap anti-correlation with valley_depth as instrument validation; sweep at dilations {6,3,1,4} so the probe arbitrates the 6/3/1-vs-6/4/1 dilation contradiction by data. A variant with valley_depth < 0.05 is classified z-blind at that dilation (recorded, informational). Wave 2 (angle 06 R2-1) added the term-decomposition mode: full/chamfer/dilated costs recorded from the same render at each sweep point (zero extra renders) — the same instrument now arbitrates the polish precondition G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1 (valley_depth ≥ 0.10; chamfer − dilated ≥ 0.05; |argmin_offset| ≤ 2 mm; min-at-zero within noise), gating the polish z-CLAIM, never the arm. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, R2-2; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, R2-1]
- Round 2 resolved contradiction 2 at the mechanism level (angle 01 R2-6): the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability at a fixed pose) are orthogonal — a variant cannot change what a fixed cost observes. Two documented second-order interactions: (i) the NaN/Inf trigger (if a cost fails on some poses, GLh changes which poses are effectively searched); (ii) refinement control (with a z-flat cost, gb/rev's suppression of the local phase during stagnation is a pure-efficiency win). The battery must report evals and z-error separately; a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-6]
- Round 2 specified the 1-DTDV boundary go/no-go: GO only if BOTH (a) the analytic probe shows 1-DTDV ≥ 1-DTC on the ν ≥ 4/6 boundary instances (Deb02 on the unperturbed [0,1]^n domain, shifted-Levy construction; the study's own ν≥8/10 rule becomes ν≥5/6 for n=6) while the interior-optimum regression stays within a pre-registered bound, AND (b) the production probe shows the pose-cost optimum at the range edge (z-profile valley argmin at the sweep edge). The depth machinery is worth it only as: occlusion-aware visibility gradients, a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm, or the z-line-integral in the ML/DRR pathway. The real z fixes are biplane (calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B + biplane branch already exist) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone) — matching the prior-run ML angle's finding 8. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "depth channel"; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70]

** Finding 5 — The cost path is sync-bound (structurally confirmed, magnitude unmeasured); 3 of 5 D2H syncs are trivially async-able, and int-atomics make bit-identical results achievable
- Per monoplane eval: ~15 kernel launches (8 render + 4 fast-implant-dilation + 3 distance-map) + 5 synchronous D2H cudaMemcpy, all on the default stream, zero streams/events anywhere in src/. The 5 syncs classify as: 2 structural mid-eval (bounding box at render_engine.cu:781–785; fragment_fill at :786–790 — removable only via kernel-level change) and 3 terminal (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289–290; distance_map_metric.cu:110–114, :115–119) — async-able now, all targets already page-locked. - The existing ms/call meter (optimizer_manager.cpp:1272–1278) uses clock() = process CPU time: it excludes GPU time AND sync-wait time, so it systematically under-reads a sync-bound pipeline and cannot arbitrate the item-8 claim. Fixing the meter (Cut 4) is required before any cut can be demonstrated to the user via the UI. Wave 2 (Finding 11) adds the 1000× unit error on top of this blind spot — Cut 4 is now a correctness fix, not polish. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The ms/call meter" + R2-1]

This resolves the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim: it applies to the DRR float-atomic path, which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Consequence: async terminal copies and iteration batching can be verified bit-identical by diffing a recorded pose→score sequence; Cut 3 (fragment-fill removal) must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. Wave 2 (angle 06 R2-4) extends the doctrine to the polish: the gradient's float accumulation MUST be an ordered two-pass reduction, because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin would trip on float-atomic accumulation. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Determinism"; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, R2-4]

Constraint: FastImplantDilationMetric writes INTO the rendered buffer, so evals must be double-buffered (second render output + duplicate score buffers); biplane gets a free overlap (secondary camera buffers are separate). [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The DIRECT loop is sequential", "In-place metric composition"]
- Round 2 (angle 04 R2-4) pinned the seam contract for the double-buffered state: compute owns the buffer STATE (second render output + duplicate score buffers), the manager owns the object GRAPH (Initialize already constructs every GPU object), the coordinator owns neither — it only registers the callback. DirectOptimizer's injection boundary stays `std::function<double(const Point6D&)>` for the single-eval path and gains ONE optional sibling `std::function<std::vector<double>(const std::vector<Point6D>&)>` (no CUDA types in the domain header); the returned vector is in input order and DirectOptimizer replays per-eval bookkeeping (cost_function_calls_++, best-value update, AddHyperBox, improvement callback) in that order, so observable values and callback order are identical whether the cost layer batches or not. All enqueue/wait/event machinery lives inside the cost callback; the mid-eval fragment-fill sync stays inside compute (its wait overlaps the previous eval's tail). Wave 2 (angle 05 R2-4) pinned the concrete situs: second renderer_output_b_ inside RenderEngine (constructed next to render_engine.cu:319) + a second score-buffer bank INSIDE GPUMetrics (dev_pixel_score_[2] / dev_distance_map_score_[2] / dev_edge_pixels_count_[2] + pinned twins, SetActiveBank(int); gpu_metrics.cu:7-65) — one object with doubled internal state, so the manager's graph (GPUMetrics constructed once at optimizer_manager.cpp:818, passed by pointer to all three CFMs) is untouched; the eval path still allocates nothing per call. ** Finding 6 — The polish stage is feasible only on a smooth surrogate; GO for chamfer-gradient polish, NO-GO for photometric/torch routes; the "12x" thesis is likely overstated
- The production DIRECT_DILATION cost is piecewise-constant in pose (binary silhouette + int reductions): finite differences on it give zero/garbage Jacobians; there is no gradient to polish through it. Published relatives: arXiv:1906.07870, arXiv:2501.14918. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "piecewise-constant", "smooth surrogate"]

Photometric DRR-intensity gradient — NO-GO for now (+3–6 weeks, low expected value). Finite-difference on the production cost — NO-GO. Torch bridge — NO-GO on design merit (autograd buys nothing for a 6-DoF static-STL scatter-add backward; torch is already linked into jtml_compute — the ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is now a resolved Cut F in angle 04, see Finding 7). Actual NaN behavior: (a) `result < current_optimum_value_` is false, so a NaN eval never updates the optimum; (b) the NaN box accumulates as dead weight (lost evals, unbounded growth); (c) the column minimum becomes NaN only after all finite boxes in that column are trisected away — delayed, conditional poisoning. ** Finding 8 — (Round 2) The NaN/Inf trigger is per-variant: DIRECT_DILATION cannot emit NaN; three other variants can; the finite-check seam belongs at EvaluateCostFunction
- Structural audit (angle 02 R2): the oracle cost is white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric + DistanceMapMetric; every intermediate is an int (ComputeSumWhitePixels int count; chamfer −1·int score; distance map int/(count+0.1) with a non-negative numerator and denominator ≥ 0.1). No float division, no sqrt, no asin, no uninitialized read; max accumulation 255·1024² ≈ 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹. Verdict: DIRECT_DILATION returns a finite double for EVERY pose, including empty silhouettes, degenerate projections, and behind-camera poses. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2 "NaN/Inf emission audit"]
- The emitters, all production-reachable: (1) DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — `if (pixel_score_ != 0)` tests the pinned pointer, never the value (implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446); with pixel_score_[0] == 0 the divisions give 0/0 NaN (selectable in production, forces dilation 3, optimizer_manager.cpp:252-253/270-271/288-289); (2) DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT — UB min_dist read can surface a NaN payload (compiler-dependent); (3) sym_trap — asin(fem2tib[2][1]) is NaN for |entry| > 1 (sym_trap_function.cpp:129), reachable through FP rounding. Int overflow and the DRR float-atomic path are ruled out. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Correction to the round-1/synthesis claim "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons": the data storage sorts each size-column descending (true minimum at the back); ConvexHull reads only the back. A NaN box fails every comparison and is inserted at the column FRONT — never selected, never popped (pops the back), never read by the hull. Actual NaN behavior: (a) `result < current_optimum_value_` is false, so a NaN eval never updates the optimum; (b) the NaN box accumulates as dead weight (lost evals, unbounded growth); (c) the column minimum becomes NaN only after all finite boxes in that column are trisected away — delayed, conditional poisoning. The finite-check is motivated by (a)+(b), not the round-1 claim. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2; src/domain/direct_data_storage.cpp:92-131]

#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1, Table 3]
- On 800 GKLS problems (n=2–5, simple+hard classes): 1-DTC-IO best average (8,021) and best median (1,427); 1-DBDP-GL ranks 5th there but is best on simple classes at budgets >400 evals; IO wins on hard GKLS classes. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 6]
- Confidence: high (directly from the study's tables; the study is the repo's own evidence base, papers/ 2022 PDF).
- Relevance: 6-DOF = n>4; 20k trunk = well above the 4000-eval crossover → GL selection is the evidence-backed choice; the partition choice is a tradeoff (1-DTC: best GKLS median + minimal change from current code; 1-DBDP: best n>4 average but requires diagonal-bisection rework). 1-DTDV is a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary.

** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]
- Performance on hidden-constraint problems (constraint info withheld, 80 problems): DIRECT-GLh failed 18/80 vs DIRECT-NAS 29/80, DIRECT-Barrier 46/80, subDIRECT-Barrier 47–53/80; GLh took ~4.5× fewer iterations and ~33× less time than NAS. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §4.2.1, Table 5]
- DirectGO's own description of why alternatives fail: NaN-valued boxes "would not be selected as potential optimal at all"; barrier penalties leave feasible-edge exploration very slow. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §2.3]
- The repo currently passes NaN/Inf straight into storage: `EvaluateCostFunction` has no finite-check; a NaN result fails `result < current_optimum_value_` so it never becomes the optimum, but NaN boxes enter the storage matrix and poison hull slopes in `ConvexHull` (NaN slope comparisons). [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L203-220, L93-141]
- Confidence: high for the algorithm and cost; medium for *whether the production GPU silhouette cost actually emits NaN* — no NaN handling exists anywhere in the C++ cost path (only Qt UI validation in app/experimental/PoseBridge.cpp L177-184), so the trigger condition is unverified.
- Relevance: if the GPU cost can fail (degenerate poses, empty silhouette), GLh converts silent corruption into a directed search toward feasibility — and the needed distance data is already there once GL selection lands.

** Finding 4: Refinement control — "restrictions hurt cheap functions" is confirmed, and -gb is the only safe one
- Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760 tested six refinement-reduction add-ons on 1-DTC-GL over 287 DIRECTGOLib v1.2 problems: success rates 1-DTC-GL-gb 0.7840 (225/287) > 1-DTC-GL 0.7805 (224/287) > -limit 0.7631 > -min 0.7526 > -rev 0.7317 > -median 0.7073 > -average 0.6551. Every restriction except gb hurt the base algorithm; gb is "the only algorithm with the same or better performance than the original 1-DTC-GL". [Source: https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf Table 2, §3, §4]
- "In the case of cheap test functions, the original 1-DTC-GL is the best of all the algorithms tested, meaning that the local refinement reduction schemes are redundant. However, when the objective functions are expensive, the local refinement reduction techniques improve the performance, and 1-DTC-GL-gb is the best technique among all tested." [Source: same, §3–§4]
- The restriction harm is worst when f_min = 0: "the restriction on selecting small hyper-rectangles may prevent the algorithms from converging to a solution... especially apparent when the solution is equal to zero" (1-DTC-GL-average worsened average evals by 32% overall; suffered most on f*=0 problems). [Source: same, §3]
- gb mechanics (from the DIRECTGO implementation of the studied algorithm): run the traditional two-step selection; after 5 consecutive iterations without f_min improvement, drop the local (distance-based) selection phase, except every 5th iteration ("security" iteration) — `(fMinNotImpr > 5) && (mod(fMinNotImpr,5) ~= 0)` → local phase else global-only. Defaults `ovexpl='GL'`, `locbalance='GL'`, `ep=1e-4`. [Source: /tmp clone of https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO, Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m L122-138, L235-237; GENDIRECT parameter table in README]
- Jones & Martins: the ε=1e-4 default protects the original DIRECT from ε=0's excessive local search; adaptive-ε (Finkel-Kelley DIRECT-restart) is mixed (better on Shubert, worse on Powell-48). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §2.3.2, §3.3]
- Confidence: high (direct quotes from the study that owns this exact question).
- Relevance: JTML's silhouette cost has f_min ≈ 0 and a GPU eval that is expensive (dilation 6/3/1 renders) — the two conditions where restrictions fail and where gb pays. ε-based restrictions (min/median/average) are doubly contraindicated (window ε|f_min| collapses at f_min→0 — the Sergeyev–Kvasov zero-minimum weakness Jones & Martins reproduce). Answer to Q3: yes, -gb is the only refinement control that survives; for cheap analytic battery functions keep it OFF and test the crossover.

** Finding 5: The full variant surface maps onto an Options struct with bit-identical defaults
- The DIRECTGO toolbox exposes exactly this surface as options: `locbalance` ∈ {GL, gb, rev} and `ovexpl` ∈ {GL, min, median, average, limit} on the I_DTC_GL family; GENDIRECT generalizes to Partitioning{Strategy: DTC/DTDV/DTCS/DBVS/DBDP/DBVD/DBC, SubSides: All/One}, Selection{AggrFuncVal, CandMeasure: Diagonal/LongSide, Strategy: Original/Aggressive/Pareto/RedPareto, EqualCand: All/One, SolRefin: Min/Median/Average/Off, Ep: 1e-4, ControlEp: Off/Restart/MultiLevel1/MultiLevel2, GloballyBiased: Off/On, TwoPhase: Off/On}. [Source: https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO README, GENDIRECT table; Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m header]
- The 12 studied variants are the cross-product IO/IA/GL × N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP; N-DTC-GL ≡ DIRECT-GL; 1-DBDP-GL ≡ GL-selected BIRECT; the study's IO and BIRECT/DIRECT differ only in the tie restriction. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §3, Table 1]

- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).

- 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.

#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). ** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]
- Performance on hidden-constraint problems (constraint info withheld, 80 problems): DIRECT-GLh failed 18/80 vs DIRECT-NAS 29/80, DIRECT-Barrier 46/80, subDIRECT-Barrier 47–53/80; GLh took ~4.5× fewer iterations and ~33× less time than NAS. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §4.2.1, Table 5]
- DirectGO's own description of why alternatives fail: NaN-valued boxes "would not be selected as potential optimal at all"; barrier penalties leave feasible-edge exploration very slow. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §2.3]
- The repo currently passes NaN/Inf straight into storage: `EvaluateCostFunction` has no finite-check; a NaN result fails `result < current_optimum_value_` so it never becomes the optimum, but NaN boxes enter the storage matrix and poison hull slopes in `ConvexHull` (NaN slope comparisons). [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L203-220, L93-141]

** Finding 4: Refinement control — "restrictions hurt cheap functions" is confirmed, and -gb is the only safe one
- Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760 tested six refinement-reduction add-ons on 1-DTC-GL over 287 DIRECTGOLib v1.2 problems: success rates 1-DTC-GL-gb 0.7840 (225/287) > 1-DTC-GL 0.7805 (224/287) > -limit 0.7631 > -min 0.7526 > -rev 0.7317 > -median 0.7073 > -average 0.6551. [Source: https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf Table 2, §3, §4]
- "In the case of cheap test functions, the original 1-DTC-GL is the best of all the algorithms tested, meaning that the local refinement reduction schemes are redundant. However, when the objective functions are expensive, the local refinement reduction techniques improve the performance, and 1-DTC-GL-gb is the best technique among all tested." [Source: same, §3–§4]
- The restriction harm is worst when f_min = 0: "the restriction on selecting small hyper-rectangles may prevent the algorithms from converging to a solution... especially apparent when the solution is equal to zero" (1-DTC-GL-average worsened average evals by 32% overall; suffered most on f*=0 problems). [Source: /tmp clone of https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO, Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m L122-138, L235-237; GENDIRECT parameter table in README]

* Variant Surface (12 + refinement add-ons)

** Selection schemes
- IO — Improved Original: lower-right convex hull of (size, f(center)) with ε in eq. (4), ties restricted to one candidate per (size,value) group. Current repo = this *without* ε and *with* all ties.
- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).
- 1-DTC — trisect the single longest side only (2 evals per POH); tie-break in the study: least-split-so-far dimension, then lowest index. Repo is 1-DTC-alike but ties break by *denormalized* side length (GetLargestDirection on denormalized sides), lowest index on equality — for anisotropic ranges (branch 15,15,25,25,25,25; leaf 3,3,15,3,3,3) the two rules diverge.
- 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.
- 1-DBDP — bisect along the diagonal, sample two interior diagonal points (reusable across descendants); best n>4 average; needs its own storage/diameter bookkeeping.

** Refinement-control add-ons (on top of GL, per Mathematics 2022)
- -min / -median / -average: ε-style floors f_min−ε|f_min|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_median|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_average| — all hurt, worst at f*=0.
- -limit: δ_limit floor (20n subdivisions in the 2022 paper) + always select the f_min box — hurt slightly (0.7805→0.7631 success).
- -gb: globally-biased two-phase switch (drop local phase after 5 non-improving iterations, security iteration every 5th) — the only non-hurting restriction; best on expensive functions.
- -rev: local phase only on the iteration f_min improves — mixed (best median, 5th success rate).
- ε=0 default in the repo vs ε=1e-4 in DIRECTGO defaults: keep 0 (current behavior) for the analytic battery baseline; the ε>0 option exists for the original-selection regime.

#+TITLE: Cost-Path Foundation: 7 Verified Bugs + Metric-Math Test Inventory
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: cost-path-foundation

* Summary

All 7 bugs are confirmed in the current source at the dispatch's line numbers, and all but two are dead for the oracle: only the DistanceMapMetric index bug (distance_map_metric.cu:27) is live in the DIRECT_DILATION cost the oracle evaluates, so the IoU 0.9936 baseline is contaminated by a deterministically-wrong distance-map term; the remaining bugs poison latent paths (DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT UB read + Y_TRANS no-op, sym_trap x→z, always-Trunk stage guard, Mahfouz pointer-guard + int truncation, curvature stub + per-stage allocation leak). The dilation contradiction resolves to code = 6/4/1 (settings_control.cpp:1201-1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h 6/−2/1; the 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json and is never exercised by the oracle's flat trunk-only budget). The backface divergence is load-bearing for the oracle: the label generator (Study2Grid) renders with culling OFF ("BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS", main.cpp:277) and the start-pose correspondence is empirically IoU==1.0 only under OFF; production OptimizerManager uses ON. Every bug gets a pin-first recipe: headless Tier-0 where a pure surface exists (transform helpers, index arithmetic, metric semantics as CPU references), Tier-2 GPU-labeled where the pin must observe the cost function itself.

* Key Findings

** Bug 1 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134: uninitialized min_dist (UB read)

- Failure mode: `double min_dist;` is declared uninitialized; the accumulation is +=-only inside `if (x_tran/y_tran/z_tran)` guards; the value is unconditionally read at `return metric_score + min_dist;` (line 159). The registry defaults for all three flags are false (CostFunctionManager.cpp listCostFunctions: X_TRANS/Y_TRANS/Z_TRANS false), so the += never executes and the return reads a fully-indeterminate double — UB ([basic.indet]). In practice the stack residue can be a signalling NaN → cost NaN → DIRECT's comparisons all false → optimizer misbehaves silently. Even with a flag true, += starts from garbage.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure, via extraction): extract the accumulation into a pure helper `double PolePenalty(x_dist, y_dist, z_dist, bool x_t, bool y_t, bool z_t, double weight)` that initializes `min_dist = 0.0` and sums only enabled axes. Spec test: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1.0,2.0,3.0,false,false,false,75.0) == 0.0)` (no flags → exactly 0 contribution) and `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1,2,3,true,false,false,75) == 75.0)`. Today the code has no such pure surface and the cost returns `metric + garbage`, so the spec test fails by construction against the current implementation (cannot link a correct helper, and the Tier-2 variant below observes the garbage).
- Pin (Tier-2 GPU-labeled, fails today): at any fixed pose with PoleWeight=0 and all flags false, `costFunctionDD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT()` must equal `white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric(...)` (the chamfer-only term, computable directly in the test via GPUMetrics). Today the return additionally carries whatever the uninitialized stack slot held. [Source: src/compute/DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134-159]
- Fix: `double min_dist = 0.0;` (line 134).
- Oracle impact: none — DIRECT_DILATION never calls this function. Confidence: high.

** Bug 2 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:117-120: Y_dist ≡ X_dist, Y_TRANS a no-op

- Failure mode: the Y-axis projection reuses the X-axis vector: `y_delX = s_x * Δx; y_delY = s_y * Δy; y_delZ = s_z * Δz;` with Δ = np−p (lines 117-119), byte-identical to the X_dist block (112-115). The Y axis of the non-principal frame is r = R·{0,1,0} = (r_x, r_y, r_z), computed at lines 93-95 and used only for alpha. Consequence: Y_TRANS toggles a duplicate of the X_TRANS term; the y-axis separation between femur and tibia is never penalized. If a user enables Y_TRANS expecting a y constraint, they silently get a double-counted x constraint.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): with identity rotation (all angles 0): r=(0,1,0), s=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1); pure y-offset Δ=(0,5,0) gives X_dist=|s·Δ|=0, correct Y_dist=|r·Δ|=5, buggy Y_dist=|s·Δ|=0. Spec test on the extracted PolePenalty: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(0, 5, 0, false, true, false, 1.0) == 5.0)`. Additionally a pure characterization on the vectors: for any pose where the s and r axes differ, `Y_dist != X_dist` must hold — today they are equal by construction. Tier-2 behavioral pin: at a pose offset purely in the non-principal y direction, toggling Y_TRANS must change the cost by `pole_weight * |r·Δ|`; today it changes nothing (Δ⊥s ⇒ X_dist=0) — fails today. Note the Tier-2 variant must run after Bug 1's fix (else min_dist garbage contaminates the delta).
- Fix: line 117-119 use r_x/r_y/r_z: `double y_delX = r_x * (np.x_location_ - p.x_location_);` etc.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 3 — CostFunctionManager.cpp:46-48: always-true stage guard collapses every stage to Trunk

- Failure mode: `if (stage_ != Stage::Trunk || stage_ != Stage::Branch || stage_ != Stage::Leaf) stage_ = Stage::Trunk;` is a tautology — no value can equal all three enum members, so the condition is always true and `stage_` is forced to Trunk after any constructor call (the Branch/Leaf constructors at settings_control.cpp:1198-1199 and any future stage-conditional logic). Live consequence today: DIRECT_DILATION_T1 (the only stage_ consumer, DIRECT_DILATION_T1.cpp:64,89) always takes its "trunk" branch and dilates the render to 1 px — its branch/leaf behavior is unreachable. DIRECT_DILATION (the oracle's cost) never reads stage_, so the oracle is unaffected.
- Pin (Tier-0, requires one test-support addition): `CostFunctionManager(Stage)` performs no GPU work in the constructor (only listCostFunctions + pointer-null init, CostFunctionManager.cpp:22-53), so a headless test can construct it and assert the stage is preserved — but `stage_` is private with no accessor (CostFunctionManager.h:147). Add `Stage getStage() const` (pure, behavior-neutral) and pin: `REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Branch).getStage() == Stage::Branch); REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Leaf).getStage() == Stage::Leaf);` — fails today (both return Trunk). Caveat: the test target must compile CostFunctionManager.cpp, which pulls CUDA headers (gpu_metrics.cuh); that is a compile-time CUDA dependency, not a runtime-GPU one — a deliberate, flagged relaxation of the "CUDA-free" headless convention for this one target (or gate the target behind JTML_BUILD_TESTS as usual, since the project already requires the CUDA toolkit to build).
- Fix: `||` → `&&` on line 46 (intent: force Trunk only for invalid values; with a 3-value enum the guard is then dead but harmless — or delete it).
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 4 — sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108: tibia transform x replaced by z

- Failure mode: the tibia transform is built as `create_312_transform(x2tib, p.z_location_, p.y_location_, p.z_location_, p.z_angle_, p.x_angle_, p.y_angle_)` — the x slot receives p.z_location_ and the z slot also receives p.z_location_. The femur call (114-118) is correct. The commented-out reference matrix at lines 91-95 shows the intent (x slot = p.x_location_). Consequence: tibia x-translation is ignored, tibia z-translation is duplicated into the x slot; fem2tib = fem2x·x2tib is corrupted → the varus/valgus angle `vv = asin(fem2tib[2][1])` and the pole distance `shortest_distance` are wrong for any pose with distinct x/z, silently corrupting both penalty terms of sym_trap.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure — genuine R13 pin on the buggy code): the transform helpers are plain CPU functions in a header (create_312_transform / invert_transformation / matmult, include/compute/sym_trap_functionCustomVariables.h:53-150). Replicate the cost's tibia call verbatim and assert the spec:
  #+begin_src cpp
  float x2tib[4][4];
  // verbatim from costFunctionsym_trap_function (pre-fix source truth):
  create_312_transform(x2tib, pose.z, pose.y, pose.z, pose.za, pose.xa, pose.ya);
  REQUIRE(x2tib[0][3] == Approx(pose.x)); // x slot must carry tibia x
  REQUIRE(x2tib[2][3] == Approx(pose.z)); // z slot must carry tibia z
  #+end_src
  With pose = (50, 20, 60, 15, -8, 30): today x2tib[0][3] == 60 (not 50) and the assertion fails; after the fix (pose.x in the x slot) it passes. A second pin builds fem2tib for femur-at-origin / tibia-(10,0,0), identity angles, and asserts the relative translation column equals (10,0,0) — today it is (0,0,0) because x slots received z=0.
- Fix: line 106 first argument `p.x_location_`.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 5 — distance_map_metric.cu:27: wrong grid→pixel index formula (LIVE in the oracle)

- Failure mode: `int i = (blockIdx.y + gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` — the block row must multiply, not add: correct is `(blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x)`. Concrete failure for a 64×64 crop with threads_per_block=256 (16×16 blocks, gridDim=(4,4)): correct block (bx,by) covers crop rows by*4..by*4+3; the buggy formula maps block (0,0) to i∈[1024,1280) ⇒ rows 16-19 instead of 0-3, block (0,1) to rows 20-23, block (1,0) ALSO to rows 20-23 — crop rows 0-15 are never visited and rows 20-23 are visited by two blocks. The only guard is `orig_loc < width*height` (line 38), so reads stay in-image but at wrong offsets (and for crops smaller than 256·gridDim rows the mapping leaves the crop entirely). Both atomicAdd counters (edge_pixel_count, distance_map_score) therefore accumulate at wrong pixels: the metric `score/(count+0.1)` is deterministic but wrong. Because DIRECT_DILATION calls DistanceMapMetric every evaluation (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), the oracle's cost landscape — and hence the IoU 0.9936 measurement — includes this corruption. This is the single bug that directly undermines the baseline.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): extract the mapping into a pure function `int CropIndexToGlobal(int blockIdxY, int gridDimX, int blockIdxX, int blockDimX, int threadIdxX)` and pin full-coverage invariants over a 64×64 crop (gridDim=(4,4), 256 threads): every crop pixel visited exactly once, none outside [0, cw*ch). The correct formula satisfies; the buggy one fails (enumerate both in the test; the failing assertion documents the bug, the passing one pins the fix). Also a Tier-2 GPU-labeled differential: DistanceMapMetric vs the CPU reference on a small synthetic image with a known edge pattern must agree; today they disagree wherever blockIdx.y > 0.
- Fix: line 27 → `int i = (blockIdx.y * gridDim.x + blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` (this matches the pattern already correct in every other metric kernel, e.g. iou.cu:37, l_1_1_matrix_diff_norm.cu:24, fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:129).
- Oracle impact: HIGH — changes the distance-map term of every oracle cost evaluation; expect the recovered pose / IoU / L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap to move. Must be followed by an oracle re-run and a baseline.json re-baseline (measured IoU 0.9936, per-px L1 0.0207 are informational, gate is IoU > 0.85). Confidence: high.

** Bug 6 — implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446 pointer guard + :93/122 double→int truncation

- Failure mode (guard): `if (pixel_score_ != 0) intensity_score = intensity_score / static_cast<double>(pixel_score_[0]);` (324) and the same at 446 for contour_score — `pixel_score_` is host-pinned memory allocated once in the GPUMetrics constructor (gpu_metrics.cu ctor cudaHostAlloc), so the pointer is never null and the guard always passes; when the denominator kernel counts zero pixels (e.g. an extreme pose with an empty silhouette crop during DIRECT exploration), the division is by 0 → ±inf/NaN cost. The intent was a value check `pixel_score_[0] != 0`.
- Failure mode (truncation): `atomicAdd(&result[0], 2.55 * pixel)` at 93 (EdgeMahfouzNumerator) and 122 (EdgeMahfouzDenominator) — `result` is `int*`, and atomicAdd(int*, int) converts the double 2.55·pixel to int with truncation toward zero (per-pixel error up to 2.55). Both the contour numerator and denominator are quantized, biasing the ratio; the intensity branch (line 153) is integer-valued already, so it is unaffected. The host then multiplies the contour numerator by 255.0 (line ~420) while the kernels' internal scale is 2.55 — a scale inconsistency that should be pinned as current spec (kernel-as-spec) and reconciled against the Mahfouz 2003 paper before "fixing".
- Pins: Tier-0 CPU reference replicates both accumulation semantics on small synthetic images — (a) the intended float/double accumulation of 2.55·pixel vs (b) the actual int-truncated accumulation, asserting they differ (documents the quantization as current behavior); Tier-2 GPU-labeled: with a rendered image whose bbox crop contains no qualifying pixels (denominator 0), `ImplantMahfouzMetric` must return a finite value (guard works) — today it can return ±inf.
- Fix: `if (pixel_score_[0] != 0)` at 324 and 446 (unambiguous bug). Truncation: default to keep-and-pin (kernel-as-spec) unless the Mahfouz paper dictates float accumulation, in which case switch the accumulators to float/double and the CPU reference becomes the spec test. Also note the final combination `contour_score * (-2.67) + intensity_score * (-1)` (line ~465) is an unnormalized weighted sum — pin as-is.
- Oracle impact: none (DIRECT_MAHFOUZ is not the oracle's cost; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ.cpp:38,50 are its only consumers). Confidence: high.

** Bug 7 — curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu: stub returning 0, plus a per-stage-init allocation leak

- Failure mode: CurvatureHausdorfMetric_Kernel (lines 17-38) computes `kp_loc` and then does nothing; the host CurvatureHeatmapMetric launches only Reset_CurvatureHausdorfScoreKernel, computes an unused `double test = 0`, and `return test;` (line 48) — constant 0.0, never reading the heatmaps, never copying dev_curvature_hausdorf_score_ back. Additional defects: crop width off-by-one `right_x - left_x - 1` (line 63, should be +1). Not registered in listCostFunctions, not called by any cost function — latent. #+TITLE: Cost-Path Foundation: 7 Verified Bugs + Metric-Math Test Inventory
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: cost-path-foundation

* Summary

All 7 bugs are confirmed in the current source at the dispatch's line numbers, and all but two are dead for the oracle: only the DistanceMapMetric index bug (distance_map_metric.cu:27) is live in the DIRECT_DILATION cost the oracle evaluates, so the IoU 0.9936 baseline is contaminated by a deterministically-wrong distance-map term; the remaining bugs poison latent paths (DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT UB read + Y_TRANS no-op, sym_trap x→z, always-Trunk stage guard, Mahfouz pointer-guard + int truncation, curvature stub + per-stage allocation leak). The dilation contradiction resolves to code = 6/4/1 (settings_control.cpp:1201-1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h 6/−2/1; the 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json and is never exercised by the oracle's flat trunk-only budget). The backface divergence is load-bearing for the oracle: the label generator (Study2Grid) renders with culling OFF ("BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS", main.cpp:277) and the start-pose correspondence is empirically IoU==1.0 only under OFF; production OptimizerManager uses ON. Every bug gets a pin-first recipe: headless Tier-0 where a pure surface exists (transform helpers, index arithmetic, metric semantics as CPU references), Tier-2 GPU-labeled where the pin must observe the cost function itself.

* Key Findings

** Bug 1 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134: uninitialized min_dist (UB read)

- Failure mode: `double min_dist;` is declared uninitialized; the accumulation is +=-only inside `if (x_tran/y_tran/z_tran)` guards; the value is unconditionally read at `return metric_score + min_dist;` (line 159). The registry defaults for all three flags are false (CostFunctionManager.cpp listCostFunctions: X_TRANS/Y_TRANS/Z_TRANS false), so the += never executes and the return reads a fully-indeterminate double — UB ([basic.indet]). In practice the stack residue can be a signalling NaN → cost NaN → DIRECT's comparisons all false → optimizer misbehaves silently. Even with a flag true, += starts from garbage.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure, via extraction): extract the accumulation into a pure helper `double PolePenalty(x_dist, y_dist, z_dist, bool x_t, bool y_t, bool z_t, double weight)` that initializes `min_dist = 0.0` and sums only enabled axes. Spec test: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1.0,2.0,3.0,false,false,false,75.0) == 0.0)` (no flags → exactly 0 contribution) and `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(1,2,3,true,false,false,75) == 75.0)`. Today the code has no such pure surface and the cost returns `metric + garbage`, so the spec test fails by construction against the current implementation (cannot link a correct helper, and the Tier-2 variant below observes the garbage).
- Pin (Tier-2 GPU-labeled, fails today): at any fixed pose with PoleWeight=0 and all flags false, `costFunctionDD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT()` must equal `white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric(...)` (the chamfer-only term, computable directly in the test via GPUMetrics). Today the return additionally carries whatever the uninitialized stack slot held. [Source: src/compute/DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134-159]
- Fix: `double min_dist = 0.0;` (line 134).
- Oracle impact: none — DIRECT_DILATION never calls this function. Confidence: high.

** Bug 2 — DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:117-120: Y_dist ≡ X_dist, Y_TRANS a no-op

- Failure mode: the Y-axis projection reuses the X-axis vector: `y_delX = s_x * Δx; y_delY = s_y * Δy; y_delZ = s_z * Δz;` with Δ = np−p (lines 117-119), byte-identical to the X_dist block (112-115). The Y axis of the non-principal frame is r = R·{0,1,0} = (r_x, r_y, r_z), computed at lines 93-95 and used only for alpha. Consequence: Y_TRANS toggles a duplicate of the X_TRANS term; the y-axis separation between femur and tibia is never penalized. If a user enables Y_TRANS expecting a y constraint, they silently get a double-counted x constraint.
- Pin (Tier-0 pure): with identity rotation (all angles 0): r=(0,1,0), s=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1); pure y-offset Δ=(0,5,0) gives X_dist=|s·Δ|=0, correct Y_dist=|r·Δ|=5, buggy Y_dist=|s·Δ|=0. Spec test on the extracted PolePenalty: `REQUIRE(PolePenalty(0, 5, 0, false, true, false, 1.0) == 5.0)`. Additionally a pure characterization on the vectors: for any pose where the s and r axes differ, `Y_dist != X_dist` must hold — today they are equal by construction. Tier-2 behavioral pin: at a pose offset purely in the non-principal y direction, toggling Y_TRANS must change the cost by `pole_weight * |r·Δ|`; today it changes nothing (Δ⊥s ⇒ X_dist=0) — fails today. Note the Tier-2 variant must run after Bug 1's fix (else min_dist garbage contaminates the delta).
- Fix: line 117-119 use r_x/r_y/r_z: `double y_delX = r_x * (np.x_location_ - p.x_location_);` etc.
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 3 — CostFunctionManager.cpp:46-48: always-true stage guard collapses every stage to Trunk

- Failure mode: `if (stage_ != Stage::Trunk || stage_ != Stage::Branch || stage_ != Stage::Leaf) stage_ = Stage::Trunk;` is a tautology — no value can equal all three enum members, so the condition is always true and `stage_` is forced to Trunk after any constructor call (the Branch/Leaf constructors at settings_control.cpp:1198-1199 and any future stage-conditional logic). Live consequence today: DIRECT_DILATION_T1 (the only stage_ consumer, DIRECT_DILATION_T1.cpp:64,89) always takes its "trunk" branch and dilates the render to 1 px — its branch/leaf behavior is unreachable. DIRECT_DILATION (the oracle's cost) never reads stage_, so the oracle is unaffected.
- Pin (Tier-0, requires one test-support addition): `CostFunctionManager(Stage)` performs no GPU work in the constructor (only listCostFunctions + pointer-null init, CostFunctionManager.cpp:22-53), so a headless test can construct it and assert the stage is preserved — but `stage_` is private with no accessor (CostFunctionManager.h:147). Add `Stage getStage() const` (pure, behavior-neutral) and pin: `REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Branch).getStage() == Stage::Branch); REQUIRE(CostFunctionManager(Stage::Leaf).getStage() == Stage::Leaf);` — fails today (both return Trunk). Caveat: the test target must compile CostFunctionManager.cpp, which pulls CUDA headers (gpu_metrics.cuh); that is a compile-time CUDA dependency, not a runtime-GPU one — a deliberate, flagged relaxation of the "CUDA-free" headless convention for this one target (or gate the target behind JTML_BUILD_TESTS as usual, since the project already requires the CUDA toolkit to build).
- Fix: `||` → `&&` on line 46 (intent: force Trunk only for invalid values; with a 3-value enum the guard is then dead but harmless — or delete it).
- Oracle impact: none. Confidence: high.

** Bug 4 — sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108: tibia transform x replaced by z

- Failure mode: the tibia transform is built as `create_312_transform(x2tib, p.z_location_, p.y_location_, p.z_location_, p.z_angle_, p.x_angle_, p.y_angle_)` — the x slot receives p.z_location_ and the z slot also receives p.z_location_. - Pin (Tier-0 pure — genuine R13 pin on the buggy code): the transform helpers are plain CPU functions in a header (create_312_transform / invert_transformation / matmult, include/compute/sym_trap_functionCustomVariables.h:53-150). Replicate the cost's tibia call verbatim and assert the spec:

  float x2tib[4][4];
  // verbatim from costFunctionsym_trap_function (pre-fix source truth):
  create_312_transform(x2tib, pose.z, pose.y, pose.z, pose.za, pose.xa, pose.ya);
  REQUIRE(x2tib[0][3] == Approx(pose.x)); // x slot must carry tibia x
