#+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). This matches the prior-run ML angle's finding 8 ("if the ML pathway is to beat the monoplane z gap, biplane is the evidence-backed direction").
- Confidence: high on the machinery facts (source-verified + NVDiffrast issue); high on the observability argument (analytic); medium on the exact clinical z-benefit of biplane/prior until measured
- Relevance: answer to accountable question 2 — the depth channel is a *gradient-quality and ablation-signal* feature, not a z fix; the harness should test it as such (self-supervised depth arm), and the z-profile probe (angle 03) should first confirm the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley — that is the precondition for any polish z-win.

** Feasibility verdicts per idea (accountable question 1 + 2, with effort/risk — accountable question 3)
- Silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO. MVP = forward-difference gradient on the surrogate (6 renders/step, ~1 week) then analytic projection Jacobian + ∇D kernel (1 render/step, +1 week), reusing Render(), the uploaded distance maps, and the injected-cost lambda. Risk medium-low: all machinery exists; the known index-formula bug in distance_map_metric.cu:27 (blockIdx.y+gridDim.x instead of blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) must NOT be copied into new kernels; float accumulation replaces int; match the production backface config (true) and leaf dilation (1) for consistency with verification.
- NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery (+1 week: min-z test + float buffer reuse), but NOT a z fix; only pursue as the enabler for occlusion-aware gradients (visibility gradients) or the synthetic-depth ablation arm. Risk low.
- Analytic AA / occlusion-aware coverage gradient (Modular-Primitives-style, 4×4-style tiles) — research increment (+2-4 weeks) after the MVP shows a win; requires the z-test ownership first. Do not start before measurement.
- Photometric DRR-intensity gradient (DiffDRR-style, hand-written CUDA) — research project (+3-6 weeks, low expected value: the gradient through the atomicAdd z-line-integral is delicate and a saturated metal implant has no usable intensity gradient in the blob interior). NO-GO for now.
- Finite-difference on the *production* cost — NO-GO (piecewise constant, see first finding).
- Torch bridge (thin autograd extension) — NO-GO on convention and merit: torch is *already linked into jtml_compute* (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib, and CostFunctionManager.h even includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>), so the dependency is not the objection — but for 6-DoF pose of a static STL, autograd buys nothing (the rasterizer backward is a scatter-add; Modular Primitives' core is a CUDA primitive library, torch is only the wrapper) and it violates the documented "no torch in the cost path" design. The ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell to flag to 04-backend-architecture. [Source: repo — src/compute/CMakeLists.txt:45, include/compute/CostFunctionManager.h, src/compute/machine_learning_tools.cpp]
- CUDA graphs — not for the polish loop: the render engine's stride/prefix/bounding-box scheme launches data-dependent grid shapes per frame (Render() computes launch sizes from fragment_fill_ on the host), which graph capture cannot freeze; that is 05-compute-perf's sync-removal territory for the *existing* path. The polish loop shares Render() unchanged, so it inherits the same 2 D2H syncs/eval — acceptable at ~10^2 polish steps but worth noting 05's win compounds here too.
- Confidence: high on the code facts; medium on effort estimates (single-dev hand-written CUDA, no per-eval timing data yet — 05 will supply it)
- Relevance: the effort/risk table the user asked for; every route reuses the injected-cost boundary and the Render() pipeline, so nothing here forks the architecture.

** The hybrid loop (accountable question 4): a 4th stage after leaf, budget-accounted, seam-unchanged for the MVP
- Loop shape: DIRECT trunk (20k) → 2× branch (5k each) → leaf (5k) → RunPolishStage(current_optimum_location_) → optional re-seed: if polish improves the production cost, run one more leaf-range DIRECT around the polished pose (the DIRECT+local-search re-seed pattern from the literature: Gablonsky's locally-biased DIRECT, the DIRECT+DF-local-search hybrids). #+TITLE: Differentiable Polish — gradient-based local refinement after DIRECT, the z-signal, and what is actually transferable to a hand-written CUDA stack
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: differentiable-polish

* Summary

A gradient-polish stage after DIRECT is feasible in this stack, but only if it optimizes a *smooth surrogate* — the production DIRECT_DILATION cost is a piecewise-constant function of pose (binary silhouette + int-atomic reductions), so its gradient is zero almost everywhere and undefined at pixel flips. The surrogate already exists in the codebase: the chamfer distance-map term (DistanceMapMetric), whose gradient is the standard analytic-silhouette-gradient: Σ over rendered edge pixels of ∇D(p)·(projection Jacobian). That Jacobian needs only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that FillTriangleKernel already computes and throws away. The depth channel is the angle's main myth to puncture: a front-surface z/w buffer is 80% machinery-present (the DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z), but a depth channel does *not* make z observable in single-plane fluoro — the 6.31 mm z gap is the magnification limit, and the only real z-fixes are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior. Verdict: GO for a budget-accounted polish stage (chamfer surrogate, analytic Jacobian, ~2-3 weeks) scored by angle 03's harness as a DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish ablation arm; NO-GO for the photometric DRR-gradient and torch-bridge routes.

* Key Findings

** The production cost is piecewise-constant in pose — the gradient of the existing cost is not a usable signal, and this is the load-bearing constraint on everything else
- FastImplantDilationMetric reduces with int atomicAdd over binary comparisons (DILATED_PIXEL/EDGE_PIXEL vs WHITE in the dilated comparison) and DistanceMapMetric sums int distance values over a *discrete* edge-pixel set; both change only when a rendered pixel flips 0↔255 as vertices cross pixel centers. The render itself (RenderEngine::Render) writes a binary silhouette. [Source: repo — src/compute/fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu, src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-92]
- Consequence: finite-difference on the production cost gives zero or garbage Jacobians for any step not straddling a flip boundary; there is no gradient to "polish" through the production metric. Any polish stage must (a) optimize a smooth surrogate, and (b) verify the result with the production cost — the surrogate is a *search* objective, the production cost stays the *arbiter* (same relationship as angle 03's appearance gate vs cost math).
- Also note the existing metric's int reduction truncates (double→int atomicAdd truncation is already listed as bug 6 in the local recon) — a polish surrogate must use float accumulation.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: kills option (b) of accountable question 1 (finite-difference on the existing cost) before it starts; forces the surrogate architecture that the harness can actually measure.

** The smooth surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a chamfer loss, and its gradient is the standard analytic silhouette gradient
- DistanceMapMetric = Σ_{rendered edge pixels} distance_map[p] / (count+0.1) — a mean-chamfer of the rendered silhouette edge to the target (fluoro) edge; the distance transform makes it Lipschitz with an image-space gradient ∇D computable numerically from the distance map itself. [Source: repo — src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu; include/compute/frame.h (SetDistanceMap)]
- The standard differentiable-registration gradient is dL/dθ = Σ_{p ∈ E(θ)} ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ) + a boundary term from pixels crossing the edge set; the boundary term is what analytic AA (Modular Primitives) or soft coverage (SoftRas/DIB-R) smooths, and it is small relative to the ∇D term inside the DIRECT basin (few flips per step at convergence). Published relatives of exactly this gradient: "Analytical Derivatives for Differentiable Renderer: 3D Pose Estimation" (arXiv:1906.07870) and "3D/2D Registration of Angiograms using Silhouette-based Differentiable Rendering" (arXiv:2501.14918). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07870; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.14918]
- dp/dθ is analytic for a rigid body: projected p = (fx·X/Z + cx, fy·Y/Z + cy) with (X,Y,Z) affine in the pose θ (R·v + t), so the 2×6 projection Jacobian is a ~50-line kernel. This is the "Modular-Primitives-style analytic silhouette gradient" in its minimal form — no soft rasterizer, no AA pass required for the MVP.
- Confidence: high (the math is standard; the codebase already contains both ingredients)
- Relevance: this is the minimal viable gradient signal (accountable question 1): analytic projection Jacobian + numerical ∇D from the existing distance map, at 1 render per step. The honest baseline to implement *first* (measurement-first) is forward/central differences on this same surrogate (6-12 renders/step, zero new rasterizer code) — it establishes whether gradient polish wins at all before the analytic investment.

** FillTriangleKernel already computes the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics that the gradient needs — and discards them
- FillTriangleKernel computes the unnormalized barycentrics (a, b, c, denominator) for the inside test and only writes 255 to the image. Writing (triangleIndex, a, b, c) out for filled pixels is the Modular-Primitives per-pixel output minus the NDC z: exactly the (ID, u, v) tuple the backward pass consumes. The renderer also knows the projected positions and (in the DRR twin) per-vertex camera z, so the un-projected 3D source point of each edge pixel is recoverable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu FillTriangleKernel; Modular Primitives rasterizer outputs (ID, u, v, zc/wc) + 2×2 barycentric Jacobian per https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2011.03277]
- Cost: one extra device buffer (float4 per filled pixel) + ~10 lines in the fill kernel. The stride/prefix/bounding-box launch scheme is untouched.
- Confidence: high (source-verified)
- Relevance: this is what makes the analytic route cheap — the rasterizer is already 80% of a differentiable rasterizer; only the output staging and the backward scatter-add are missing.

** The depth channel: machinery is 80% present, but a depth channel does NOT fix the z-weak axis in single-plane fluoro — the honest finding this angle exists to deliver
- Where z comes from today: the silhouette path (Render) computes per-vertex camera z (tZ) in WorldToPixelKernel and *discards it*; the DRR path stores it (dev_transf_vertex_zs_) and DRR_FillTriangleKernel interpolates per-pixel perspective-correct z via the rational formula (tvz1·tvz2·tvz3·denominator)/(a·tvz2·tvz3 + b·tvz1·tvz3 + c·tvz1·tvz2) — which is exactly 1/(λ1/z1 + λ2/z2 + λ3/z3), i.e. the perspective-correct interpolated camera z at the pixel. There is no z-testing anywhere (all triangles draw; backfaces are sign-flipped in the DRR accumulation). A front-surface NDC-style depth buffer (this stack's "z/w" ≡ −tZ_cam, positive toward the detector) needs only a min-z test in the fill + a float buffer — and dev_z_line_values_ (width×height float) is already allocated and reusable. [Source: repo — src/compute/render_engine.cu:430-520, src/compute/render_drr_engine.cu DRR_WorldToPixelKernel + DRR_FillTriangleKernel, include/compute/render_engine.cuh dev_z_line_values_/dev_transf_vertex_zs_]
- Why it does not fix z: (a) there is *no target depth* in a single-plane fluoro to compare a rendered depth against — a depth-difference term only exists in synthetic self-supervised ablations (render at known pose → optimize), against a registered bone model / known-geometry prior, or in biplane; (b) the observed z gap is the magnification limit — z-translation is only observable through scale (6.31 mm z gap vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane in baseline.json; angle 03's probe arithmetic: <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m), and no gradient changes what is observable; (c) NVDiffrast — the reference implementation of Modular Primitives — intentionally does *not* backprop through the z/w channel (issue #70: the z/w output's gradients are not propagated; the meaningful gradients are the vertex-position ones). [Source: repo — test/golden/baseline.json tolerances.observed_max_gap_vs_golden; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70 (search-verified content, page fetch failed); https://nvlabs.github.io/nvdiffrast/]
- What the depth machinery IS worth: (i) occlusion-aware visibility gradients — Modular Primitives' premise "a 3D primitive with no effect on the image receives zero gradient" requires knowing which triangle owns each pixel (z-test), which the renderer lacks today; (ii) a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm (a genuine z test *when a target depth exists*); (iii) the z-line-integral (dev_z_line_values_) is a stronger quantitative z signal than front-depth (it shifts by ≈Δz·path-length under z-translation) but is an X-ray-attenuation proxy — unobservable for a saturated metal implant and only useful in the ML/DRR pathway (DiffDRR-style).
- The real z-fixes: biplane (the codebase already has it — calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B and a biplane branch in DIRECT_DILATION) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone). #+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 3 (wave 1 complete) — angles 01–04 carry '## Round 3' sections grounded in Zotero primary texts; angles 05–06 remain round-2 complete (rounds: 1 = all six; 2 wave 1 = 01–04; 2 wave 2 = 05–06; 3 wave 1 = 01–04)
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

** Finding 6 — The polish stage is feasible only on a smooth surrogate; GO for chamfer-gradient polish, NO-GO for photometric/torch routes; the "12x" thesis is likely overstated
- The production DIRECT_DILATION cost is piecewise-constant in pose (binary silhouette + int reductions): finite differences on it give zero/garbage Jacobians; there is no gradient to polish through it. The surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a mean-chamfer loss with a Lipschitz image-space gradient ∇D, and its analytic gradient is the standard silhouette gradient dL/dθ = Σ ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ), needing only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics FillTriangleKernel already computes and discards (~10 lines + one float4 buffer to stage them). Published relatives: arXiv:1906.07870, arXiv:2501.14918. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "piecewise-constant", "smooth surrogate"]
- Feasibility verdicts: silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO (MVP = forward differences, 6 renders/step ~1 week; then analytic Jacobian + ∇D kernel, 1 render/step, +1 week; reuses Render(), uploaded distance maps, injected-cost lambda; float accumulation; match production backface=true and leaf dilation 1). NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery but NOT a z fix; only as occlusion/ablation enabler. Analytic AA / occlusion-aware gradients — research increment after the MVP shows a win. Photometric DRR-intensity gradient — NO-GO for now (+3–6 weeks, low expected value). Finite-difference on the production cost — NO-GO. Torch bridge — NO-GO on design merit (autograd buys nothing for a 6-DoF static-STL scatter-add backward; torch is already linked into jtml_compute — the ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is now a resolved Cut F in angle 04, see Finding 7). ** Finding 8 — (Round 2) The NaN/Inf trigger is per-variant: DIRECT_DILATION cannot emit NaN; three other variants can; the finite-check seam belongs at EvaluateCostFunction
- Structural audit (angle 02 R2): the oracle cost is white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric + DistanceMapMetric; every intermediate is an int (ComputeSumWhitePixels int count; chamfer −1·int score; distance map int/(count+0.1) with a non-negative numerator and denominator ≥ 0.1). No float division, no sqrt, no asin, no uninitialized read; max accumulation 255·1024² ≈ 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹. Verdict: DIRECT_DILATION returns a finite double for EVERY pose, including empty silhouettes, degenerate projections, and behind-camera poses. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2 "NaN/Inf emission audit"]
- The emitters, all production-reachable: (1) DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — `if (pixel_score_ != 0)` tests the pinned pointer, never the value (implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446); with pixel_score_[0] == 0 the divisions give 0/0 NaN (selectable in production, forces dilation 3, optimizer_manager.cpp:252-253/270-271/288-289); (2) DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT — UB min_dist read can surface a NaN payload (compiler-dependent); (3) sym_trap — asin(fem2tib[2][1]) is NaN for |entry| > 1 (sym_trap_function.cpp:129), reachable through FP rounding. Int overflow and the DRR float-atomic path are ruled out. Round 3 (angle 02 R3-1): the Mahfouz 2003 paper confirms the emitter's metric structure (two predicted-sum-normalized ratios, contour > intensity, negative weights, 3-px band) and that the paper's original optimizer was SA-modified Nelder-Mead (the repo deliberately runs DIRECT instead, implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:248-250) — no new emitter information; the 0/0 NaN path stands as the one real production-reachable emitter, and the value-guard fix proceeds. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2 + R3-1]
- Correction to the round-1/synthesis claim "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons": the data storage sorts each size-column descending (true minimum at the back); ConvexHull reads only the back. A NaN box fails every comparison and is inserted at the column FRONT — never selected, never popped (pops the back), never read by the hull. Actual NaN behavior: (a) `result < current_optimum_value_` is false, so a NaN eval never updates the optimum; (b) the NaN box accumulates as dead weight (lost evals, unbounded growth); (c) the column minimum becomes NaN only after all finite boxes in that column are trisected away — delayed, conditional poisoning. The finite-check is motivated by (a)+(b), not the round-1 claim. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2; src/domain/direct_data_storage.cpp:92-131]
- The finite-check wraps DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205) — the single chokepoint shared by production (RunDirectStage), the oracle, and the coordinator; CUDA-free (headless-testable), one std::isfinite per eval. Design: `if (!std::isfinite(result)) { non_finite_count_++; /* GLh: result = f_min + d(x,x_min) when enabled; else treat as infeasible (do not store, never wins the optimum) */ }` plus GetNonFiniteCount() and an iteration-callback event. The GPU side needs NO checks — all GPU outputs are provably finite ints. Probes: Tier-0 headless (fake cost lambda returning NaN/±Inf/sNaN; asserts no crash, counter increments, optimum never reflects a non-finite eval, GLh surrogate behavior, surviving columns finite) and Tier-2 GPU (sanity sweep golden ± range ~61 evals; adversarial poses ±200 mm off-axis, behind camera, 90°/180° rotations; assert finite AND cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess after each eval — the sticky-error trap at render_engine.cu:713; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ at an empty-silhouette pose EXPECT NaN today, green after the guard fix). Six failure modes code-grounded (degenerate projection, zero denominator, empty silhouette, uninitialized memory, fragment overflow = mute evals, int overflow ruled out). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Cross-angle consequence: GLh's trigger question (angle 01 Finding 3) is answered — the trigger exists but only outside the oracle's cost, so GLh is conditional on the three emitters, and the finite-check is justified on its own (a latent bug class), independent of GLh. Round 3: the GLh formula itself is now paper-verified (Finding 3), so the finite-check/feasibility-flag landing spec is fully determined: f_min over FEASIBLE columns only; store raw f_min + d; normalize at selection by (f_max−f_min) and √n; re-tag when x_min moves ≥ 1e-6 (unit coords); Emmental-GKLS is the validation battery. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-4/R3-1; angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]

** Finding 11 — (Round 2 wave 2) The ms/call meter has a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot; Cut 4 is a correctness fix, not polish

On Linux glibc, clock() returns microseconds (CLOCKS_PER_SEC = 1e6; MSVC uses 1000). The code labels the value "ms/call"; the actual value is CPU-µs/call → a 1000× unit error. The JTA codebase is a Windows-Qt origin, so this is plausibly port-induced, but on this Linux/pixi build the error is live. Severity: medium-high for the meter's purpose (user-facing speed/ETA are wrong by ~3 orders of magnitude; no before/after perf claim through this meter is meaningful); high as a correctness fact. Confidence: high (code path verified; the platform unit semantics are POSIX-standard; the "port-induced" attribution is medium). [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1]

** Standing rules that survive every step
- IoU ≥ 0.85 is the appearance arbiter, never raw pose (DIRECT convergence is noisy by design); z-gap is a recorded band (15.0 mm informational), not a gate — the lineage's own convention (JTA success excludes z; Jensen/Arulampalam report z as the weakest axis); the banded L1 gate waits for the noise-floor protocol (N ≥ 5 repeats per GPU, pooled σ, band recorded in baseline.json as a re-baseline event).
- Pin-first: every change is preceded by a characterization pin; defaults reproduce today's behavior bit-identically (R13). The perturbation suite keeps the gate honest: it must contain at least one injection that fails, one that passes, and one whose outcome is a measurement — and (Round 3) it must mirror the corpus's sensitivity analyses (Flood's dilation/Canny tables, Jensen's ambiguous zone) so its checked coverage is field-anchored, not first-principles-only.
- One jj commit per logical change; no interactive pagers.
- The OptimizerRunDriver seam and the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda are the shared vocabulary — the oracle, the probe, the polish stage, and the perf meter all consume them; nothing re-owns them.
- Allocations: the eval path performs no cudaMalloc/cudaHostAlloc/free today — keep it that way across all cuts (all targets are already pinned; the polish's gradient partials and attribute buffer are allocated once at stage init, off the eval path).
- gb semantics and the split rule are recorded in the ablation manifest as variant dimensions (which semantics, which rule) — the harness must know exactly which variant it measured. Round 3: the same manifest discipline now covers dilation_semantics {bilateral|render-only}, dilation_lineage {code|docs|flood-femur|flood-tibia}, the Canny config {0/150, 40/120, 30/80}, the z-stage budget, and ε per run.
- Determinism is non-negotiable across all three workstreams: int-atomic cost reductions for the perf cuts, ordered (non-atomic) float reduction for the polish gradient, run_hash + rerun_identical as the twin — a change that breaks bit-identity where claimed fails its gate (Contradiction 3, extended).
- The meter is a measurement instrument, not a display: Cut 4's true-ms/call output is a precondition for demonstrating ANY perf or variant win to the user (Finding 11).
- Round 3: the z-stage budget is a manifest parameter, not a constant (Flood's 50k vs JTML's 5k is an ablation axis, not a fact to argue); the multi-stage oracle's stage-bookkeeping gate extends to the flood-direct-jta caps when that shape is exercised.

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+ROUND: 3 (wave 1 complete) — angles 01–04 carry '## Round 3' sections grounded in Zotero primary texts; angles 05–06 remain round-2 complete (rounds: 1 = all six; 2 wave 1 = 01–04; 2 wave 2 = 05–06; 3 wave 1 = 01–04)
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

Round 2 wave 2 added two more high-value deliverables on top of the wave-1 deepening. **First, the ms/call meter carries a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot**: grep finds zero CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere in src/ — both meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame and :1272-1279 iteration callback) divide raw clock() ticks by calls and label the result "ms/call"; on Linux glibc clock() returns microseconds, so the value is CPU-µs/call labeled as ms/call. The UI compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) reads the µs value as ms → IPS understated ~1000×, and the ETA (:4598/:4659) is overstated by the same factor. This is a correctness fact, not polish — no before/after perf claim through the existing meter is meaningful, and Cut 4 (now a full spec for BOTH sites) must emit true ms/call so the existing UI math becomes correct without UI changes. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1/R2-2] **Second, the polish stage is now an executable MVP spec with its own falsifiable preconditions**: a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the same 31 renders, pre-registered thresholds G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1), a forward-difference arm (7 renders/accepted step, ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), an analytic arm (1 render/step via the 2×6 projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel, with an ordered two-pass float reduction so the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin cannot trip), and a **three-arm study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k budget-gift control, C: DIRECT@34k + polish@1000)** that arbitrates the 12x-vs-1.5–3x contradiction without confounding "polish quality" with "budget reallocation". [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org R2-1/R2-2/R2-4/R2-5]

Round 3 (wave 1) moved the run's evidentiary base onto the primary texts: angles 01–04 re-verified their round-1/2 conclusions against the Zotero corpus (Flood 2018, Mahfouz 2003, Jones 1993, Gablonsky 2001, Jensen 2024, Yamazaki 2004, the DIRECTGO / DIRECT-GLh / 2022-study papers, Burton, Arulampalam) and **resolved three open contradictions outright**. (1) **Mahfouz normalization**: the paper corroborates the kernel's structure (two predicted-sum-normalized ratios, contour weighted more heavily, negative weights, a 3-px capture band — a full lineage match) but the numeric weights are unextractable (embedded PDF equations), so the kernel-as-spec verdict keeps 2.55/×255/−2.67/−1 and only the pointer-guard fix proceeds. (2) **Three-way dilation contradiction**: Flood's constants are now verbatim — femur 10/6/1, tibia 6/2/1, branch = trunk−4, leaf = 1; leaf=1 is unanimous, trunk 6 (code AND docs) is the paper's TIBIA value applied to a FEMUR (femur robust band 8–12), and BOTH 6/4/1 and 6/3/1 violate branch=trunk−4 — so the dilation-schedule ablation now tests the lineage configs {10,6,1}, {6,2,1}, {6,4,1}, {6,3,1} plus a bilateral-vs-render-only semantics axis. (3) **GLh formula**: verified from the paper itself (raw surrogate f_min + d stored, selection-time normalized d̃ = d/√n with f̃_min ≡ 0, f̃=1 flat case, 1e-6 recompute threshold, Definition-1 feasibility detection) with a ready-made constrained battery (Emmental-GKLS, 100/100 solved by GLh in the paper). One description-level correction matters for every downstream number: **the oracle's DIRECT_DILATION cost chases the dilated Canny edges of the fluoroscopy frame, not the Study2Grid label — only the IoU/L1 gate uses the label** — so the Canny config (oracle 3/0/150 vs production 3/40/120 vs paper femur-A 3/30/80) is cost-load-bearing, and the Phase-2 re-baseline must stay single-variable (index fix only). [Sources: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org R3-1/R3-2/R3-3/R3-5; angles/01-direct-variants.org R3-1]

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and now fully specified in content, with the Round-3 deltas folded in: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh; the re-baseline stays single-variable with the Canny config pinned, per Finding 12); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe (now with the lineage dilation-schedule sweep, a Yamazaki-polynomial mode, and a coupling mode) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam (now with the z-stage budget as a FIRST-CLASS parameter — Flood's 50k z-evals vs JTML's 5k, and the flood-direct-jta budget shape; three pins replace the stale "seam addition"); (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite mirroring the corpus's own sensitivity analyses — Flood's dilation/Canny tables, Jensen's ambiguous zone — and a benchmarks block with regime tags); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with the paper-verified GLh formula, an ε-arm {0, 1e-7, 1e-4}, the DGO battery protocol (two-tier ε_pe, data profiles, 13/80 caveat, Emmental-GKLS), and a STAGED battery metric (trunk basin-capture + per-stage refinement) that matches the lineage's already-forfeited cross-stage global convergence; (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, with Cut 0's first-run record now carrying the lineage-throughput reconciliation (~3,000 evals/s on a 2018 GTX 970 vs JTML's derived 20–60); (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06 — the executable MVP (chamfer-surrogate gradient, precondition gate G1–G4, FD then analytic arms) arbitrated by the three-arm study, with the Yamazaki-style decoupled z-polish as the field-validated z-remedy candidate and the matched-projector doctrine carried over from LEAP. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F, with the convergence-tradeoff design note placed in the stage-script TU (cover is a stage-loop property; Options carries no cover knob).

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. Round 3 adds the lineage's own confirmation: Flood's success metric excludes z by definition ("out-of-plane translation is not considered in our definition of success"), the z-stage exists explicitly "because it is the least accurate degree of freedom for single-plane fluoroscopy", and the field's z-accuracy band (Yamazaki 2.6–3.2 mm conventional → 0.9–1.8 mm remedied; Jensen out-of-plane < 1.8 mm; Arulampalam depth MAE 1.8 mm) frames JTML's measured 6.31 mm as a candidate regression — the multi-stage oracle and probe are the instruments that decide. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state, and the polish gradient must use an ordered (non-atomic) float reduction because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin would trip on float-atomic accumulation.

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

Round 2 sharpened the critical path in an important way: the corrupted index has **exactly one reader** (DistanceMapMetric_Kernel, invoked only from DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:80), and every post-optimize measurement metric (IoU, per-px L1, chamfer) uses the correct formula — so the 0.9936/0.0207 numbers themselves are not corrupted, only the cost that drove the search. The corruption is a systematic exclusion: the top ~64 crop rows of the rendered band are never sampled and the middle band is multiplicity-over-weighted, so the distance-map term is *flatter in z* than the honest chamfer complement. The structural prediction is that the re-baselined DIRECT optimum moves toward the golden z and the frame-1 6.31 mm z gap shrinks materially (direction: medium-high confidence; magnitude: not predictable without the GPU re-run).

Round 2 wave 2 added two more high-value deliverables on top of the wave-1 deepening. **First, the ms/call meter carries a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of its CPU-time blind spot**: grep finds zero CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere in src/ — both meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame and :1272-1279 iteration callback) divide raw clock() ticks by calls and label the result "ms/call"; on Linux glibc clock() returns microseconds, so the value is CPU-µs/call labeled as ms/call. The UI compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) reads the µs value as ms → IPS understated ~1000×, and the ETA (:4598/:4659) is overstated by the same factor. This is a correctness fact, not polish — no before/after perf claim through the existing meter is meaningful, and Cut 4 (now a full spec for BOTH sites) must emit true ms/call so the existing UI math becomes correct without UI changes. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org R2-1/R2-2] **Second, the polish stage is now an executable MVP spec with its own falsifiable preconditions**: a term-decomposed z-profile probe (chamfer-only vs dilated-overlap-only valley depths from the same 31 renders, pre-registered thresholds G1–G4 at leaf dilation 1), a forward-difference arm (7 renders/accepted step, ~140 steps within B_p = 1000), an analytic arm (1 render/step via the 2×6 projection Jacobian + gradient-of-distance-map kernel, with an ordered two-pass float reduction so the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin cannot trip), and a **three-arm study (A: DIRECT@35k, B: DIRECT@34k budget-gift control, C: DIRECT@34k + polish@1000)** that arbitrates the 12x-vs-1.5–3x contradiction without confounding "polish quality" with "budget reallocation". [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org R2-1/R2-2/R2-4/R2-5]

Round 3 (wave 1) moved the run's evidentiary base onto the primary texts: angles 01–04 re-verified their round-1/2 conclusions against the Zotero corpus (Flood 2018, Mahfouz 2003, Jones 1993, Gablonsky 2001, Jensen 2024, Yamazaki 2004, the DIRECTGO / DIRECT-GLh / 2022-study papers, Burton, Arulampalam) and **resolved three open contradictions outright**. (1) **Mahfouz normalization**: the paper corroborates the kernel's structure (two predicted-sum-normalized ratios, contour weighted more heavily, negative weights, a 3-px capture band — a full lineage match) but the numeric weights are unextractable (embedded PDF equations), so the kernel-as-spec verdict keeps 2.55/×255/−2.67/−1 and only the pointer-guard fix proceeds. (2) **Three-way dilation contradiction**: Flood's constants are now verbatim — femur 10/6/1, tibia 6/2/1, branch = trunk−4, leaf = 1; leaf=1 is unanimous, trunk 6 (code AND docs) is the paper's TIBIA value applied to a FEMUR (femur robust band 8–12), and BOTH 6/4/1 and 6/3/1 violate branch=trunk−4 — so the dilation-schedule ablation now tests the lineage configs {10,6,1}, {6,2,1}, {6,4,1}, {6,3,1} plus a bilateral-vs-render-only semantics axis. (3) **GLh formula**: verified from the paper itself (raw surrogate f_min + d stored, selection-time normalized d̃ = d/√n with f̃_min ≡ 0, f̃=1 flat case, 1e-6 recompute threshold, Definition-1 feasibility detection) with a ready-made constrained battery (Emmental-GKLS, 100/100 solved by GLh in the paper). One description-level correction matters for every downstream number: **the oracle's DIRECT_DILATION cost chases the dilated Canny edges of the fluoroscopy frame, not the Study2Grid label — only the IoU/L1 gate uses the label** — so the Canny config (oracle 3/0/150 vs production 3/40/120 vs paper femur-A 3/30/80) is cost-load-bearing, and the Phase-2 re-baseline must stay single-variable (index fix only). [Sources: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org R3-1/R3-2/R3-3/R3-5; angles/01-direct-variants.org R3-1]

The recommended course of action, in dependency order, is unchanged in shape and now fully specified in content, with the Round-3 deltas folded in: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, behavior-neutral fixes, the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline — plus the CUDA-free finite-check at DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction, needed regardless of GLh; the re-baseline stays single-variable with the Canny config pinned, per Finding 12); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe (now with the lineage dilation-schedule sweep, a Yamazaki-polynomial mode, and a coupling mode) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam (now with the z-stage budget as a FIRST-CLASS parameter — Flood's 50k z-evals vs JTML's 5k, and the flood-direct-jta budget shape; three pins replace the stale "seam addition"); (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json (schema now complete, plus the perturbation suite mirroring the corpus's own sensitivity analyses — Flood's dilation/Canny tables, Jensen's ambiguous zone — and a benchmarks block with regime tags); (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** — now with the paper-verified GLh formula, an ε-arm {0, 1e-7, 1e-4}, the DGO battery protocol (two-tier ε_pe, data profiles, 13/80 caveat, Emmental-GKLS), and a STAGED battery metric (trunk basin-capture + per-stage refinement) that matches the lineage's already-forfeited cross-stage global convergence; (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, with Cut 0's first-run record now carrying the lineage-throughput reconciliation (~3,000 evals/s on a 2018 GTX 970 vs JTML's derived 20–60); (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06 — the executable MVP (chamfer-surrogate gradient, precondition gate G1–G4, FD then analytic arms) arbitrated by the three-arm study, with the Yamazaki-style decoupled z-polish as the field-validated z-remedy candidate and the matched-projector doctrine carried over from LEAP. Architecture work (angle 04) flows through as additive cuts A–F, with the convergence-tradeoff design note placed in the stage-script TU (cover is a stage-loop property; Options carries no cover knob).

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: the variant choice (search scheme) and the z-sensitivity ranking (cost observability) are orthogonal in mechanism, with only two documented second-order interactions (the NaN/Inf trigger and refinement-control savings on z-flat costs); the harness must report evals and z-error separately, and a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix. Round 3 adds the lineage's own confirmation: Flood's success metric excludes z by definition ("out-of-plane translation is not considered in our definition of success"), the z-stage exists explicitly "because it is the least accurate degree of freedom for single-plane fluoroscopy", and the field's z-accuracy band (Yamazaki 2.6–3.2 mm conventional → 0.9–1.8 mm remedied; Jensen out-of-plane < 1.8 mm; Arulampalam depth MAE 1.8 mm) frames JTML's measured 6.31 mm as a candidate regression — the multi-stage oracle and probe are the instruments that decide. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results; angle 04's seam contract pins the double-buffered eval state, and the polish gradient must use an ordered (non-atomic) float reduction because the ablation runner's rerun_identical determinism twin would trip on float-atomic accumulation.
